$comment: Cross-fragment changes the QA pass on 20-board.json (board subsystem) could not apply itself. Section 8 of docs/CHECKLIST.md: merging a node in another fragment, merging into anything under c64.bottoms-out (metal.*, chem.*, industry.*), renaming anything another fragment references, and changing an id are proposals, not edits. Applied centrally by the maintainer.

merges.why: THE ACTIONABLE HALF. chem.rosin (70-petrochem, category packaging, reached from chem.solder-chemicals) and metal.rosin (60-metals, category metals) are the same substance published twice, and metal.rosin currently sits unreferenced in unlinked.catalogue. Merge metal.rosin into chem.rosin. My side is already clean: 20-board.json used to carry a third copy as mb.solder.wire.core.colophony (+ .stumps, .acid); that is deleted and the solder wire now reaches rosin through chem.rosin.

This duplicate surfaced while auditing my own `from` resolution: the bare ingredient string 'caustic soda' was resolving by name to the caustic-soda node buried inside the compressed-air branch, which is nonsense as an ingredient. mb.pcb.strip now names metal.caustic-soda explicitly so the bad link is gone, but both nodes are still published and still compete on the name 'Caustic soda'. Merge, or rename one.

Two natural-gas nodes: chem.natural-gas 'Natural gas: the gas field' (composition, sources, processing, uses) and facility.power.natural-gas (North Sea, LNG, US domestic). CHECKLIST 1a names chem.natural-gas as the cross-cutting gas stream, so it should be the survivor; fold the pipeline/LNG/US supply branches into it. My mb.pcb.laminate.press.heat reads `from: chem.natural-gas`.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (the whole 15-node subtree is deleted; mb.pcb.laminate now contains chem.glass-fiber by id). Filed so the reviewer can see the decision. chem.glass-fiber in 55-chem-gaps.json is the richer node (E-glass composition, batch mixing, regenerative melt with the 10-40 h conditioning step, bushing, attenuation, weaving, filter grades) and my copy repeated the same chain one level down. It was also sitting unreferenced in unlinked.catalogue; it is now properly linked from the board.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (19 nodes deleted). mb.pcb.laminate now contains chem.epoxy.dgeba and chem.epoxy.brominated-epoxy by id. My copy reproduced the bisphenol-A/cumene/phenol, epichlorohydrin/chlorohydrin/brine and tetrabromobisphenol-A chains that chem.epoxy already owns, and it duplicated chem.epoxy.branched-epoxy's brominated-cresol-novolac point. Nothing was lost that the canonical node does not already say.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (mb.pcb.foil, .ed, .ed.nodule, .wind deleted). metal.copper.foil owns both the ED drum route (metal.copper.foil.ed-drum, including the bonding treatment) and the rolled-annealed alternative. SEPARATE FACTUAL NOTE FOR THE METALS OWNER, since I am not allowed to edit that file: metal.copper.foil's description says 'the C64's board is single-sided, so it is one sheet of foil laminated to 1.6 mm FR-4'. That is wrong for this board - ASSY 250407 is two-layer, 35 um copper on both faces, no vias.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE, and it is a relation fix as much as a merge. The edge was a `children` edge to the alias id chem.ferric-chloride, which build.mjs rewrites to chem.pcb-chemicals.etching.ferric-chloride. An etchant is an ingredient of an etching operation, not a component inside it, so the child edge is gone and mb.pcb.etch now carries `from: chem.pcb-chemicals.etching.ferric-chloride`. mb.pcb.finish.hasl lost its `children: chem.solder` edge the same way, in favour of `from: metal.solder`.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (16 nodes deleted). metal.solder in 60-metals.json is the canonical 63/37 node and already owns the ingot route, metal.solder.alloy-making (cored-wire method, antimony), metal.solder.wire, metal.solder.wave-solder, metal.solder.pot and metal.solder.cleaning. My alloy/bar/wire chain repeated the tin-and-lead split, the bar casting and the wire drawing, and my colophony chain repeated chem.rosin. mb.solder now carries `from: metal.solder, chem.rosin` and the branch is about the machines and the joints rather than the metal. Note the residual overlap: my mb.solder.wave is the capital equipment while metal.solder.wave-solder and metal.solder.pot are the same activity written as processes - that one is fine as a tool/process pair, but see the next entry for the cleaning step.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (3 nodes deleted: mb.assembly.resistors, .networks, .film). The carbon-film element and the resistor networks are owned by 30-passives.json; mine were a path-local copy with no part numbers, on top of a node that described a subject rather than an operation. mb.assembly's description now points at mb.passives.resistors.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE. 80-industry.json publishes the sprung probe pin (2.54 mm grid, 100-300 g contact force, tungsten-rhenium or beryllium copper) as facility.test-equipment.needle-probe. My three-node copy is deleted; mb.test.ict.tester references the shared probe.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (shadow mask and Invar deleted). The test monitor only has to be a monitor; the CRT mask and Invar chain belongs to the television branch that 90-peripherals.json already writes. mb.test.video.monitor now says so in its note.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (6 nodes deleted: .element, .nickel, .ore, .mine, .chrome, .chromite). The burn-in heating element is nichrome, so that branch was a duplicate nickel-and-chromium path. mb.test.burnin.oven now carries `from: metal.nickel, metal.chromium`. Four further copies of iron-ore-and-coke inside my own fragment (mb.pcb.laminate.press.pigiron/ironore/orebody, mb.solder.wave.frame.iron/ore, mb.assembly.insertion.engine.iron/ironore/orebody/coke/coalseam, mb.test.functional.cradle.ore/coalseam) went the same way and now converge on metal.hematite and metal.coke.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (4 nodes deleted: .wall, .nickel, .nickel.ore, .nickel.body). The pot wall was a path-local stainless-and-nickel copy; metal.stainless.304 is canonical. WORTH WATCHING: 30-passives.json has 'nickel' in mb.passives.resistors.inputs, and that string was resolving by name onto my deleted mb.solder.wave.pot.wall.nickel. After the deletion it resolves to metal.nickel, which is the right answer - but it is a name-heuristic resolution, so it will move again if anyone adds a node called 'Nickel'. The same fragility applies to 'caustic soda', 'chlorine', 'screen' and 'propylene' anywhere else in the tree.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (3 nodes deleted). Wolframite ore behind a carbide drawing die duplicated the scheelite/wolframite vein node in 60-metals.json. SIDE FINDING: data/_ingredients.json maps 'tungsten wire' to metal.tungsten, and metal.tungsten does not exist in the tree, so that lookup silently produces nothing. Publish metal.tungsten or repoint the table entry; I am not editing that file.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (node deleted; mb.pcb.laminate.press.hydraulic now carries `from: chem.refining.products.lubricants`). The local 'Hydraulic oil' node was tagged category energy, which is the catch-all misuse CHECKLIST section 3 warns about.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (6 nodes deleted: .base, .base.eg, .base.eg.ethylene, .base.naphtha, .base.crude, .base.reservoir). The artwork film base is PET and chem.polyester.pet owns the ethylene-glycol and terephthalic-acid sides. mb.photo.plotter.film and mb.pcb.photoresist.carrier now both read `from: chem.polyester.pet`. Three separate local copies of 'crude oil -> petroleum reservoir' also existed in this fragment and all three are gone.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (4 nodes deleted: .aromatic, .naphtha, .crude, .reservoir). Hydroquinone is made from benzene and chem.styrene.benzene is the benzene node; my fourth copy of the crude chain went with it. mb.photo.develop.developer now carries `from: chem.styrene.benzene`.

ALREADY APPLIED ON MY SIDE (node deleted). A part-flavoured node called 'The RF modulator as a separate daughterboard' was sitting under a note about the absence of reflow, which is two things at once and belonged to neither. The RF modulator has a full subtree of its own in 50-power.json (mb.rf-modulator, schematic 251025/251696, 63.6 x 62.6 x 24 mm module), so the fact is now a sentence in mb.assembly.reflow's description instead of being a second, worse copy of it.

CROSS-REFERENCE, NOT A MERGE - please do not apply this one as a merge. The same step (washing rosin flux residue off a soldered board) is written twice: as an assembly operation in this fragment and as a waste-stream problem in 60-metals.json. Both readings earn their place, so this wants one node with two aspects, or at minimum a cross-link. Both are left in place and mb.assembly.cleaning's note says so.

note:
What I did to data/20-board.json, for the record. Node count 238 -> 108. No id was changed, so nothing outside this file needed rewriting: I checked every other fragment and none of them referenced any id in 20-board.json. All 108 nodes are reachable from mb.pcb / mb.solder / mb.assembly / mb.test / mb.photo.

AUDIT. node scripts/build.mjs exits 0. node scripts/audit.mjs --file 20-board.json examines 108 nodes and reports none of my own mechanical failures, and 24 warnings, all of them one heuristic: a tool, a part or a note sitting in the `assembly` or `logistics` category, where audit.mjs's CAT_OK table admits only `process`. I left those alone on purpose - a wave-soldering machine, a bed of nails and a test cradle are assembly equipment, and `assembly` is the only permitted bucket that fits them. Recategorising them into `metals` or `industry` to silence a warning would be a lie. The four FAILs the audit still prints are tree-wide rule 1a checks for 'Water for a factory', 'Electricity at the factory wall', 'Natural gas: the gas field' and 'Petroleum: light sour crude oil'. I fixed all four edges that were mine - mb.pcb.strip and mb.assembly.cleaning on water, mb.solder.hand and mb.solder.wave.preheat.air on electricity. The remaining 16 + 31 + 12 + 24 offending parents are all in other fragments and belong to their owners.

INGREDIENT LINKS. All 112 input strings across 73 nodes are now exact node ids, so every one resolves on the first try: no name matching, no _ingredients.json table, no prose left dangling. Before this pass: 'electricity' matched nothing at all in 14 places, because the node is a `facility` and build.mjs only indexes part and material names; 'caustic soda' resolved to facility.compressed-air.caustic-soda; 'chlorine' resolved to chem.polycarbonate.phosgene.chlorine; 'screen' resolved to c64.psu.transformer.winding.screen - an interwinding earth screen inside a transformer - on both the solder-mask and the silkscreen steps; 'nickel' resolved to a node inside my own solder-pot subtree; 'propylene' resolved to a propylene node buried in 10-silicon.json's mould-compound branch.

VERIFIED FINDINGS, all preserved. Zero vias and zero plated-through holes; exactly two wire jumpers, E1 and E2; no SMT and no reflow; no conformal coating; HASL as the period pad finish; boards made in Hong Kong; ASSY 250407 / fab 250406 / artwork 251137 / schematic 251138; roughly 1200 unplated holes. The empty 'no plated-barrel line' branch is still there and is now kind note rather than a process, so it reads as a recorded absence instead of an unfinished step.
